data.rationale: The commit ensures that when eval_const_expressions simplifies COALESCE, CASE, or NULLIF expressions to a single input argument, it correctly preserves the original expression's typmod and collation using RelabelType. This is specifically triggered when COALESCE has a leading NOT NULL argument, CASE has a constant condition, or NULLIF has a constant NULL second argument. The grammar fragment introduces alternatives that favor these constant or NOT NULL inputs combined with explicit COLLATE clauses. These constructs are frequently used in collation-sensitive contexts like GROUP BY or ORDER BY, where a failure to preserve collation would lead to incorrect results or plan-time errors.
data.grammar_fragment: expr<text> : <0.5> ( expr<text> COLLATE collation ) | <0.5> COALESCE "(" @col(text) "," ( expr<text> COLLATE collation ) ")" | <0.5> NULLIF "(" expr<text> "," ( "NULL::text" COLLATE collation ) ")" ; collation : '"C"' | '"POSIX"' ; expr<T> : <0.5> CASE WHEN "true" THEN expr<T> ELSE ( expr<T> ) END | <0.5> CASE WHEN "false" THEN expr<T> ELSE expr<T> END ;
seeds: CREATE TABLE t_simpl (a text NOT NULL, b text); INSERT INTO t_simpl VALUES ('foo'), ('FOO'); SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT COALESCE(a, b COLLATE "C") FROM t_simpl GROUP BY 1) q;

CREATE TABLE t_simpl_case (a text NOT NULL); INSERT INTO t_simpl_case VALUES ('abc'), ('ABC'); SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN true THEN a ELSE 'x' COLLATE "C" END FROM t_simpl_case GROUP BY 1) q;
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT NULLIF(c1, NULL::text COLLATE "POSIX") FROM t0 GROUP BY 1) q;

rewrites.name: nullif_null_id
rewrites.why: NULLIF with a constant NULL second argument reduces to the first argument; the commit ensures typmod and collation are preserved during this reduction.

rewrites.name: case_true_id
rewrites.template: CASE WHEN true THEN {e} ELSE 0 END
rewrites.why: A CASE expression with a constant TRUE condition reduces to the result of the THEN branch.

rewrites.name: coalesce_self_id
rewrites.why: COALESCE with two identical arguments reduces to the first; this checks if the reduction logic correctly handles metadata when simplification occurs.
